method: symmetric four-world authoring, post-hoc seeded key selection

worlds.keyAct: expresses relief and states when the card will be collected
worlds.line: Someone handed your keycard in at the desk last night.
worlds.reply: That's a relief. I'll pick it up before class.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports that the missing card has been recovered and is waiting at the desk. The reply that expresses relief and says the card will be collected before class treats it as retrievable, which is exactly what the report makes it. The reply that resolves to pay for a replacement assumes the card is still gone; the reply naming a side entrance answers a question about where the card was used that nobody asked; the reply agreeing to fill in a slip if one is passed over assumes a form has been offered.

kills.1: The desk says the card was 'handed your keycard in' last night, so buying a replacement today would be paying for something already sitting on the counter.
kills.2: Because the card was 'handed your keycard in at the desk', nothing has been asked about doors, and naming the side entrance responds to a question that was never put.
kills.3: 'Someone handed your keycard in' is an announcement, not an offer of a lost-property form, so agreeing to fill one in has nothing to attach to.

worlds.keyAct: resolves to buy a replacement
worlds.line: Nobody's turned your keycard in, I'm afraid.
worlds.reply: Then I'd better pay for a replacement today.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line closes off the possibility that the card will come back on its own. The reply that resolves to pay for a replacement today takes the only route left once nothing has been handed in. The reply about collecting the card before class assumes there is something to collect; the reply naming a side entrance answers an unasked question about where it was used; the reply about filling in a slip if one is passed over assumes a form was offered rather than a dead end reported.

kills.0: Since 'Nobody's turned your keycard in', there is nothing at the desk to pick up before class.
kills.2: 'Nobody's turned your keycard in' reports an outcome rather than asking anything, so naming the entrance where it was used answers nothing.
kills.3: With 'Nobody's turned' the card in, no lost-property form has been produced or requested, so agreeing to complete one on the spot comes out of nowhere.

worlds.keyAct: answers a factual question about where the card was last used
worlds.line: Do you remember which door you last used it on?
worlds.reply: The side entrance by the bike racks, late morning.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line asks the student to place the card's last known use. The reply naming the side entrance by the bike racks supplies exactly the location the question is fishing for. The reply about collecting the card before class assumes it has already been found; the reply resolving to pay for a replacement jumps past a search still in progress; the reply agreeing to fill in a slip if one is passed over responds to a request that was not made.

kills.0: 'Do you remember which door' is a question about the search, not word that the card is waiting to be picked up before class.
kills.1: Asking 'which door you last used it on' means the search is still live, so paying for a replacement today abandons a question still being worked through.
kills.3: 'Do you remember which door' asks for information, not for a lost-property form to be completed.

worlds.keyAct: agrees to complete the form and asks for it to be handed over
worlds.line: Can you fill out a lost-property slip for me?
worlds.reply: Sure, pass one over and I'll do it here.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line asks the student to complete a piece of paperwork. The reply agreeing and asking for the slip to be passed over does the task where the request placed it, at the desk. The reply about collecting the card before class assumes it has turned up; the reply resolving to pay for a replacement treats a paperwork request as a verdict; the reply naming the side entrance answers a question about doors that was never asked.

kills.0: Being asked to 'fill out a lost-property slip' means the card has not surfaced, so there is nothing to pick up before class.
kills.1: 'Can you fill out' a form is a request for paperwork, not notice that a replacement must now be bought.
kills.2: A request for 'a lost-property slip for me' asks nothing about which door was used, so naming the side entrance leaves the request unanswered.

worlds.keyAct: acknowledges the outcome and undertakes to brief the roommates
worlds.line: I've logged it as an informal first warning.
worlds.reply: Understood. I'll let my roommates know where we stand.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line states how the noise report has been recorded, at the lowest level and internally. The reply that acknowledges it and undertakes to brief the roommates fits an outcome that concerns the room but calls for no defence. The reply about putting a side of it in writing assumes something formal is under way; the reply accepting mediation and offering evenings takes up an offer that was not made; the reply about getting back late and the noise having stopped answers a question about presence that was never asked.

kills.1: Because it has been logged as 'an informal first warning', there is no formal process to submit a written account to.
kills.2: 'I've logged it' reports an action already taken, not an offer to sit both rooms down, so accepting and naming evenings takes up something that was never offered.
kills.3: An 'informal first warning' being logged asks nothing about who was in the room, so describing a late return answers a question that was not put.

worlds.keyAct: resolves to submit a written account
worlds.line: It's gone up to the housing coordinator as a formal complaint.
worlds.reply: Then I'd better put my side of it in writing.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports that the matter has escalated out of the corridor and into an official channel. The reply resolving to put a side of it in writing meets a formal process with the kind of response a formal process takes. The reply undertaking to brief the roommates treats it as a private heads-up; the reply accepting mediation and naming evenings responds to an offer of help that was not made; the reply about getting back late answers an unasked question about who was present.

kills.0: Once it has 'gone up to the housing coordinator', telling the roommates where things stand understates a matter that is no longer being handled in the corridor.
kills.2: 'As a formal complaint' is the opposite of a proposal to mediate, so accepting mediation and offering evenings responds to something that was not offered.
kills.3: A report that it has 'gone up to the housing coordinator' asks nothing, so an account of getting back late answers a question that was never asked.

worlds.keyAct: accepts the offer of mediation and supplies availability
worlds.line: I can sit down with both rooms and mediate.
worlds.reply: I'd take you up on that; evenings suit us.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line offers to bring the two rooms together with the RA present. The reply accepting and saying evenings suit takes the offer and moves it towards a time, which is what an offer of a meeting needs. The reply undertaking to brief the roommates treats an offer as a verdict; the reply about putting a side of it in writing assumes a formal complaint exists; the reply about getting back late answers a question about presence that was not asked.

kills.0: 'I can sit down' offers something ahead, not a decision already recorded, so telling the roommates where things stand skips over the offer without answering it.
kills.1: An offer to 'sit down with both rooms' is not a formal proceeding, so writing up one side of it responds to a process that does not exist here.
kills.3: Offering to 'sit down with both rooms and mediate' asks nothing about who was in the room, so describing a late return leaves the offer hanging.

worlds.keyAct: answers a question about whether the student was present
worlds.line: Were you even in the room when it got loud?
worlds.reply: No, I got back late and it had already stopped.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line asks whether the student was actually there while the noise was happening. The reply saying he got back late and it had already stopped answers the question directly and places him outside the window in question. The reply undertaking to brief the roommates treats a question as an outcome; the reply about putting a side in writing assumes a formal complaint; the reply accepting mediation and offering evenings takes up an offer that was not made.

kills.0: 'Were you even in the room' is a question, not a decision about how the report was logged, so undertaking to tell the roommates where things stand answers nothing.
kills.1: Asking 'Were you even in the room' establishes no formal complaint, so resolving to put a written side together responds to a process nobody has started.
kills.2: 'when it got loud' is asking about the night itself, not offering to sit the rooms down, so accepting mediation and naming evenings misses the question.

worlds.keyAct: states a drying workaround
worlds.line: The dryer's out again and the parts haven't shipped.
worlds.reply: I'll start hanging things on my rack, then.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports the dryer down with no repair in sight. The reply about hanging things on a rack adopts the only drying method left while the machine stays out. The reply asking about the card system assumes the dryer is running; the reply promising to set an alarm responds to a request to clear a load that was not made; the reply about bringing towels down takes up an offer of shared space that was not made.

kills.1: With 'The dryer's out again', asking whether it is back on the same card system assumes a machine that is not running.
kills.2: 'the parts haven't shipped' is a report, not a request to clear a finished load, so promising an alarm answers a request nobody made.
kills.3: Since 'The dryer's out again', there is no load of anyone's for towels to go in with.

worlds.keyAct: asks a follow-up question about how the machine is paid for
worlds.line: They got the dryer running again this morning.
worlds.reply: Is it back on the same card system?
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports the dryer repaired and back in service. The reply asking whether it is back on the same card system is the practical next thing to know about a machine you are about to use again. The reply about hanging things on a rack assumes it is still broken; the reply promising an alarm answers a request to clear a load that was not made; the reply about bringing towels down accepts an offer of shared space that was not made.

kills.0: 'They got the dryer running again' removes the reason to fall back on a drying rack.
kills.2: 'running again this morning' is news about the machine, not a request to shift a finished load, so promising to set an alarm responds to nothing that was asked.
kills.3: Reporting that 'They got the dryer running' offers no share of anyone's load, so bringing towels down takes up an offer that was not made.

worlds.keyAct: agrees to clear the machine promptly
worlds.line: Could you shift your load out when it finishes?
worlds.reply: Of course — I'll set an alarm for it.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line asks the student to clear the machine as soon as the cycle ends. The reply agreeing and saying an alarm will be set solves the actual difficulty in that request, which is being there at the right moment. The reply about hanging things on a rack assumes the dryer is broken; the reply asking about the card system responds to news of a repair; the reply about bringing towels down accepts an offer of shared space that was not made.

kills.0: 'Could you shift your load out' presupposes a machine that is working, so switching to a drying rack answers a breakdown that has not been reported.
kills.1: Being asked to move a load 'when it finishes' is not news of a repair, so asking whether it is back on the same card system responds to something unsaid.
kills.3: 'Could you shift your load out' is a request to clear space, not an offer to share a load, so bringing towels down inverts what was asked.

worlds.keyAct: accepts the offer of space in another load
worlds.line: You can put your towels in with my load.
worlds.reply: That'd save me a trip; I'll bring them down.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line offers the student space in a load that is already going in. The reply saying it saves a trip and undertaking to bring the towels down accepts the offer and does the one thing acceptance requires. The reply about a drying rack assumes the dryer is out; the reply asking about the card system responds to a repair report; the reply promising an alarm answers a request to clear a machine that was not made.

kills.0: 'You can put your towels in' presupposes a working machine, so falling back on a drying rack answers a breakdown that has not happened.
kills.1: 'in with my load' is an offer of space, not a report that the dryer was fixed, so asking about the card system responds to news nobody gave.
kills.2: Being told 'You can put your towels in with my load' is an offer, not a request to clear the machine, so promising an alarm answers the wrong thing.

worlds.keyAct: arranges for the named recipient to come and claim it
worlds.line: Your parcel's here but it's under your roommate's name.
worlds.reply: I'll ask her to come down with her ID.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports the parcel present but addressed to someone else in the room. The reply about asking the roommate to come down with her ID solves precisely the mismatch between who is standing there and whose name is on the label. The reply about booking a redelivery assumes the parcel has left; the reply about signing before the desk closes assumes the student can claim it himself; the reply saying nothing has been told about since then answers a question about other deliveries that was not asked.

kills.1: 'Your parcel's here' means it has not gone anywhere, so booking a redelivery online arranges the return of something already on the shelf.
kills.2: Because it is 'under your roommate's name', signing for it before the desk closes runs straight into the name problem the line raises.
kills.3: 'Your parcel's here' is a statement about one item, not a question about what else has arrived, so reporting nothing since then answers nobody.

worlds.keyAct: arranges a redelivery
worlds.line: The carrier took your parcel back to the depot.
worlds.reply: I'll book a redelivery on their site tonight.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports that the parcel is no longer in the building and has gone back to the carrier. The reply about booking a redelivery on the carrier's site handles a parcel sitting at a depot, which is where the line puts it. The reply about the roommate coming down with ID assumes the parcel is on the shelf; the reply about signing before the desk closes assumes the same; the reply saying nothing has been told about since then answers an unasked question about other deliveries.

kills.0: Since 'The carrier took your parcel back', bringing the roommate down with ID would produce a name for a parcel that is not in the building.
kills.2: 'back to the depot' means there is nothing at the desk to sign for before it closes.
kills.3: 'The carrier took your parcel' reports what happened rather than asking what else has come, so reporting nothing since then answers no question.

worlds.keyAct: commits to signing for it before the desk closes
worlds.line: Your parcel came in on the early van today.
worlds.reply: I'll sign for it before the desk closes.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports the parcel delivered and available now. The reply committing to sign for it before the desk closes claims a parcel that is sitting there under the student's own name. The reply about the roommate coming down with ID assumes a name mismatch nobody mentioned; the reply about booking a redelivery assumes the parcel has gone back; the reply saying nothing has been told about since then answers a question about other deliveries that was not asked.

kills.0: 'Your parcel came in' names no one else, so fetching the roommate and her ID invents an ownership problem the line does not raise.
kills.1: Because it 'came in on the early van today', a redelivery would be booked for something that has already arrived.
kills.3: 'Your parcel came in on the early van' is news of an arrival, not a question about what else has come, so reporting nothing since then answers nothing.

worlds.keyAct: answers a question about other deliveries
worlds.line: Has anything else of yours arrived since Friday?
worlds.reply: Nothing that I've been told about since then.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line asks whether further items have come in over the last few days. The reply saying nothing has been told about since then answers the span the question covers. The reply about the roommate coming down with ID responds to a name problem nobody raised; the reply about booking a redelivery assumes a parcel went back to a depot; the reply about signing before the desk closes claims an item nobody said was there.

kills.0: 'Has anything else of yours arrived' asks a question and names no roommate, so sending her down with ID answers a problem that was not raised.
kills.1: Asking whether anything 'arrived since Friday' says nothing about a parcel going back, so booking a redelivery responds to a return nobody reported.
kills.2: 'Has anything else of yours arrived' does not report an item waiting, so undertaking to sign for it before the desk closes claims something unmentioned.

worlds.keyAct: restores the cupboard now that the job is done
worlds.line: It was just a loose washer, so it's sorted.
worlds.reply: Good, then I'll put everything back under the sink.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports a small fault, already fixed, with no further work needed. The reply putting everything back under the sink is what you do when a job has finished and the space is yours again. The reply about clearing the cupboard before the technician returns assumes another visit; the reply about using the tap down the hall assumes this one must stay off; the reply about the damp patch assumes the leak was traced somewhere else entirely.

kills.1: 'so it's sorted' means there is no return visit to clear the cupboard for.
kills.2: Since it was 'just a loose washer' and the job is done, there is no reason to walk down the hall for another tap.
kills.3: 'It was just a loose washer' locates the fault at the sink itself, so treating a wall stain as explained points at a source the line rules out.

worlds.keyAct: prepares the space for the bigger job
worlds.line: The pipework's corroded, the whole trap needs replacing.
worlds.reply: I'll clear the cupboard before you come back.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line reports a fault too large to finish today and names the part that has to be swapped. The reply clearing the cupboard before the technician comes back prepares for the return visit that a trap replacement implies. The reply putting everything back under the sink assumes the job is finished; the reply about a tap down the hall answers a request that was not made; the reply about the damp patch assumes the source was found behind the wall.

kills.0: 'the whole trap needs replacing' means the work is not finished, so restocking the cupboard now just has to be undone.
kills.2: 'The pipework's corroded' reports a diagnosis, not a request to leave the tap alone, so going down the hall answers an instruction nobody gave.
kills.3: Since the fault is that 'The pipework's corroded' at the sink, treating a damp wall patch as explained points somewhere the line does not.

worlds.keyAct: agrees to leave the tap alone and names the alternative used meanwhile
worlds.line: Can you keep that tap off until I return?
worlds.reply: No problem, I'll use the one down the hall.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line asks the student not to run that tap until the technician is back. The reply agreeing and saying the one down the hall will be used shows how the request will actually be kept. The reply putting things back under the sink assumes the work is over; the reply clearing the cupboard responds to a diagnosis nobody gave; the reply about the damp patch treats the request as a finding about the radiator.

kills.0: 'until I return' says the visit is not over, so restocking the cupboard under the sink acts on a completion that has not happened.
kills.1: 'Can you keep that tap off' is a request, not a report that a part has failed, so emptying the cupboard responds to a diagnosis nobody gave.
kills.3: Being asked to 'keep that tap off' names no other source, so treating a damp wall patch as explained draws a conclusion the request does not offer.

worlds.keyAct: connects the corrected diagnosis to something already noticed
worlds.line: It's the radiator behind it leaking, not the sink.
worlds.reply: That explains the damp patch on that wall.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line corrects the assumed source of the water, moving it from the sink to the radiator behind it. The reply about the damp patch on that wall follows the correction to something the student had already noticed and could not account for. The reply putting everything back under the sink treats the visit as closed; the reply clearing the cupboard prepares for sink work the line has just ruled out; the reply about the tap down the hall answers a request that was not made.

kills.0: 'It's the radiator behind it leaking' announces a live fault, so putting everything back under the sink treats an unfinished problem as closed.
kills.1: Because it is 'not the sink', clearing the cupboard under it prepares for work the correction has just moved elsewhere.
kills.2: 'It's the radiator behind it leaking' is a correction, not a request about the tap, so going down the hall complies with an instruction nobody gave.

worlds.reply: Tuesday it is — I'll have the room straight.
worlds.explanationIfSpoken: The line gives the window during which rooms will be checked, without saying anything about this room's condition. The reply fixing on the start day and undertaking to have the room straight treats the earliest possible day as the one to be ready for. The reply about the shelves staying put assumes a pass has already been given; the reply asking whether removing the wedge is enough assumes a fail; the reply claiming the recycling answers a question about the corridor that was not asked.
